purpose: Richard Morton source-linked editorial timeline candidate database
notes: This is a research document only. No timeline entries are auto-published. All archive images remain locally private.

timeline.title: From the North East to London
timeline.detail: According to Wikipedia, Richard moved to London after playing in rock bands; avoid exact year unless he confirms.

timeline.title: The Panic Brothers form
timeline.detail: Richard forms a close-harmony comic duo with Reg Meuross, initially appearing on the London pub-rock circuit.
timeline.evidence: Wikipedia; University of Kent collection history

timeline.title: The early Panic Brothers
timeline.detail: Early publicity photograph, and reported appearances including the GLC Farewell Festival. Link date to image only after checking original.
timeline.evidence: Archive filename; Wikipedia source for GLC event

timeline.title: In The Red and Edinburgh
timeline.detail: The Panic Brothers release mini-LP In The Red and appear at Edinburgh; the Kent catalogue lists four items for 1987, including Panic Brothers flyers and festival ephemera.

timeline.title: Friday Night Live
timeline.detail: The Panic Brothers appear on Friday Night Live, alongside further festival activity.
timeline.evidence: British Comedy Guide, year 1988; archive filename
timeline.status: strong TV credit; photo year to check

timeline.title: The Panic Brothers Hold Their Own
timeline.detail: Their own Edinburgh show is reported in Wikipedia; archive includes Edinburgh 1989 publicity.

timeline.title: A new solo comedy chapter
timeline.detail: The Panic Brothers part ways and Richard develops his solo musical stand-up career, including Cutting Edge.

timeline.title: Time Out Comedy Award
timeline.detail: Richard wins a 1992 Time Out Comedy Award, recognising his songs, comedy and collaborations.

timeline.title: Edinburgh and the Jack Dee tours
timeline.detail: Festival appearances and Jack Dee tour publicity appear in the archive.

timeline.title: A headline tour and major venues
timeline.detail: Kent independently records Richard's first solo headline tour in 1994; an Apollo marquee photograph names him as Jack Dee's special guest.

timeline.title: Theatre, touring and television
timeline.detail: Tour publicity with Jo Brand and Lee Evans; Wikipedia discusses mid-nineties television work. Our Friends in the North was produced before its 1996 transmission, so do not describe 1995 as its broadcast year.
timeline.evidence: Archive; Wikipedia (production), broadcasting date needs dedicated check

timeline.title: Edinburgh and Newcastle
timeline.detail: Posters from the Edinburgh and Newcastle comedy festivals.

timeline.title: Comedy Store television special
timeline.detail: Wikipedia dates Richard's Channel 5 Comedy Store Special to 1997; archive includes a Lee Evans UK tour image and a Time Out/Radio 4 item.
timeline.evidence: Wikipedia; Kent mid-nineties TV summary; archive

timeline.title: Stand Up Two and Never Mind The Buzzcocks
timeline.detail: British Comedy Guide lists both 1998 BBC Radio 2 Stand Up Two as host and Never Mind The Buzzcocks appearance.
images: BBC RADIO 2, HOST OF STAND UP 2 '98.jpeg

timeline.title: Comedy tours continue
timeline.detail: Archive publicity featuring Phill Jupitus and a UK tour with Junior Simpson.

timeline.title: More years at Edinburgh
timeline.detail: Wikipedia describes regular Edinburgh work through 2001; the archive includes 2001 Edinburgh/tour artwork.

timeline.title: The early 2000s
timeline.detail: An undifferentiated image labelled 2002 exists. Do not invent a milestone until its contents are reviewed.

timeline.title: The Theme That Never Was
timeline.detail: Richard and Dave O'Brien's instrumental-film-and-TV-theme concept album. Wikipedia says the collaboration developed around 2010, but other catalogues list 2009 or an October 2010 release date. Confirm original release history.
timeline.evidence: Wikipedia; Word of Books; D.O.C. records conflicting years

timeline.title: In The Lounge With Rich Morton
timeline.detail: A BBC Radio 4 documentary on lounge music written/presented by Richard; episode link supplied directly by Richard.
timeline.evidence: BBC programme b01cwszp; Wikipedia; radio listings

timeline.title: I Can't Stand Up for Falling Down
timeline.detail: BBC Radio 4 documentary, and Wikipedia dates the follow-up Rich Morton Sound album The Sequel That Never Was to 2013. Confirm album publication year.
timeline.evidence: BBC b038c0f4; Wikipedia; potential retail metadata discrepancy

timeline.title: Panic Brothers reunion
timeline.detail: The duo reunites, coinciding with remastered album release.
timeline.evidence: British Comedy Guide Return of the Panic Brothers 2014; Wikipedia

timeline.title: The Lost Art of the TV Theme
timeline.detail: Richard's BBC Radio 4 documentary examines enduring television theme music and its changing role.

timeline.title: Fred At The Stand
timeline.detail: Richard appears in the BBC At The Stand series.

timeline.title: Colour Me Groovy becomes a real BBC theme
timeline.detail: Written as an imaginary theme, Colour Me Groovy was commissioned for Bennett Arron Worries About... and adopted by Chris McCausland's You Heard It Here First. Richard's 2026 first-person social post reports three series of the latter by March 2026.
timeline.evidence: Richard's own BBC RADIO THEME MUSIC.jpg; British Comedy Guide; BBC Radio 4 programme listings
timeline.status: strong use, check exact commissioning dates

timeline.title: Bennett Arron's Big Welsh Con
timeline.detail: Richard's own November 2026 post states he supplied the music for Bennett Arron's BBC Radio Wales series, with an accompanying YouTube clip.
timeline.evidence: Richard's own BBC Radio Wales this month, Nov 2026.png; BBC programme schedules
timeline.status: strong current event; avoid unverified episode details
